new_jobs.title: Internal Acceleration, Research Engineer (Kernels)
new_jobs.description:
Job Summary

Our Internal Acceleration team’s mandate is to build agents to accelerate the production of frontier tokens.

You’ll work directly with our founders and embed with our kernels team to build new agentic harnesses and operating systems to transform the way hardware is built in an AI native world. You’ll work on harnesses, tool use, context, and memory, execution environments, and evals that let agents conduct long-running engineering work that is useful.

This role is for engineers who thrive on ambiguity, have real product sense, and want to own problems end to end. It’s a whiteboard for future founders. The problems we solve are time-sensitive and business-critical. This role will not be a 9-5, and the ideal candidate is excited about that.

You may be a good fit if you

Have at least 1-5+ years of experience building and shipping software end to end, ideally at a fast-moving startup
Have built agents for complex, multi-step tasks that people depend on, beyond calling an API: tool design, long-context management, evals, and failure analysis.
Are a strong software engineer who has built reliable systems others depend on, such as distributed systems, experiment infrastructure, or developer tooling.
Use coding agents heavily, read their transcripts closely, and change the system when an agent is confidently wrong.
Have high agency in unfamiliar domains. You find the real problem and drive it forward.
Have product sense, design taste, and extreme attention to detail

Key Responsibilities

Embed with our kernels team to find the highest-leverage bottlenecks, and own each one from first idea to a tool engineers rely on every day.
Build and deploy LLM agents wired into our engineering workflows via tool-calling and MCP.
Build execution environments where agents can verify their own work, with sandboxed access to simulators, EDA flows, compilers, profilers, and real hardware.
Ship full-stack internal products from zero to one: the interfaces, data pipelines, and infrastructure that define how Etched builds.
Measure what works. Design evals and track adoption so we double down on the tools that matter and kill the ones that don’t.
Take on special projects directly with the founders, surfacing problems across the company and doing whatever it takes to hit critical milestones.

Strong candidates may also have

Exposure to chip development, kernels, hardware, or manufacturing.
Infrastructure, data engineering, or DevOps experience
Fine-tuning, RAG over proprietary technical data, or multi-agent orchestration
Startup experience, especially through hypergrowth

Benefits

Medical, dental, and vision packages with generous premium coverage
$500 per month credit for waiving medical benefits

Housing subsidy of $2,500 per month for those living within walking distance of the office
Relocation support for those moving to San Jose (Santana Row)
Various wellness benefits covering fitness, mental health, and more
Daily lunch and dinner in our office
Unlimited compute budget subject to ROI justification

Base Compensation Range

$150K – $400K+
Plus Significant Equity

How we’re different

Etched believes in the Bitter Lesson. We are the first inference-focused frontier AI system, betting early on transformer and transformer-like architectures and on increasing model sizes. Our addressable market is the entirety of inference, unlike many of our competitors.

We are a fully in-person team in San Jose (Santana Row), and greatly value engineering skills. We do not have boundaries between engineering and research, and we expect all of our technical staff to contribute to both and work across disciplines as needed.

About Etched

Etched is building hardware for frontier intelligence. We co-design chips, racks, software, and manufacturing to deliver best-in-class throughput and latency across both prefill and decode workloads. Our first products are heavily focused on inference. Backed by hundreds of millions from top-tier investors and staffed by leading engineers, Etched is redefining the infrastructure layer for the fastest growing industry in history.

Compensation Range: $150K - $400K

new_jobs.title: Sr. Product Designer, AWS Applied AI Solutions
new_jobs.description:
Description

Amazon Connect Talent is an AI-powered hiring and talent assessment platform. It conducts AI-led interviews, runs adaptive assessments, and produces structured evaluations at the scale of high-volume hiring, built on the same hiring science Amazon uses for its own seasonal workforce. It reached general availability in 2026 and is now in the phase where the experience, not the capability, decides whether customers trust it. We are looking for a Senior Product Designer to lead the mobile-first, AI-native candidate experience for Amazon Connect Talent.

Two Things Make This Role Unusual

The AI does the interview. You will not be designing a form that an AI scores afterward. You will be designing an experience where the system conducts a conversation, adapts what it asks based on what it has heard, and produces an evaluation that affects whether someone gets a job. That means designing for non-determinism: what the system does on its own and what it asks permission for, how it signals that it is listening and understanding, what happens when it mishears or misjudges, how a candidate corrects it, and how someone comes to trust a process with no human on the other end. These decisions are made with engineering and data science, not handed to them.

The phone is the product. For a high-volume candidate there is no desktop fallback. The experience has to work one-handed, on cellular, in a single sitting, under the stress of being evaluated. We are designing mobile-first in the real sense, the constraints of that context shape the product decisions rather than getting accommodated at the end.

You will also work the way our team has found to be fastest: prototype first. Our strongest delivery path on this product has been a designer building a working, AI-coded prototype to drive the discussion, then partnering with a design technologist to productionize it. It has shipped real experiences in weeks without drawing on core engineering capacity. We are looking for someone who works this way naturally, who reaches for a running prototype rather than a static comp when a question is genuinely open, and who knows when the prototype has answered the question and craft has to take over.

Key job responsibilities

Lead the mobile-first, AI-native candidate experience for Amazon Connect Talent end to end.
Co-own AI behavior with engineering and data science: how the system conducts and adapts an interview, surfaces uncertainty, fails gracefully, and earns calibrated trust.
Design for a high-volume candidate interviewing on their own device, treating that context as the primary constraint, not a responsive adaptation.
Build AI-coded prototypes to resolve open questions and drive alignment.
Set the standard for when AI-generated work is acceptable and when hand-craft is required, and raise the team's AI fluency.
Frame problems as much as solve them: surface risks others have not, and drive clarity when strategy is still forming.
Establish interaction and visual standards that hold as the product grows, designing for longevity rather than launch.
Influence partner teams across product, engineering and data science, and be the designer those leaders seek out on product decisions.
Default to a recommendation: take a clear position, argue it with data, and defend it to senior leadership.
Prioritize ruthlessly, balancing short- and long-term customer needs, and connect design work to measurable results.
Mentor designers, improving their craft and AI fluency.

About The Team

The design team for Connect Talent sits inside AWS Applied AI Solutions, covering the products in our portfolio that have shipped but are not yet mature. These are surfaces with live customers, real usage data, and the hardest design questions still open.

Basic Qualifications

7+ years of design experience
Experience carrying design concepts through exploration, development, and into deployment or mass production
Experience developing, deploying and managing AI products at scale
Experience with prototyping and implementation
Experience in designing for both mobile and desktop applications.
Experience building complex software systems that have been successfully delivered to customers, or experience designing or architecting (design patterns, reliability and scaling) of new and existing systems
Experience working with technical and product stakeholders to define requirements, prioritize features, and influence product roadmaps

Preferred Qualifications

Experience designing and executing online customer experiences

Company Description:
Nexus is building the Self-Improving OS for manufacturing. Our platform seamlessly embeds Industrial Agents into decades-old equipment and proprietary industrial control systems to monitor production lines, trace every loss to its root cause, and autonomously act.
We're growing quickly, with customers ranging from Fortune 100 manufacturers to startups building cutting-edge supply chains in the United States. Our team is comprised of manufacturing and software experts from Tesla, Distyl, and Convoy, and we're backed by A*, a16z, BoxGroup, and more.

Overview:
We're looking for a Forward Deployed Engineer to own AI Agent strategy and implementation inside some of the largest manufacturing environments in the country. You'll work at the bleeding edge of AI and your work will directly drive the creation of physical products across the economy.

There is no other place in the world to do this job the way you'll do it here. At Nexus, a forward deployed engineer works across entire industries and verticals of manufacturing, from solar cell and energy infrastructure to CPG. You'll manage multiple clients, and within them multiple plants, sites, factories, and implementations, with billions of dollars' worth of product flowing through the areas you touch. You’ll see throughlines across product development, scalable optimizations, and entire industries that no one sitting inside a single plant/customer could. And you'll be able to take learnings from one deployment and apply them across every customer we serve.

What You'll Do:
Own the customer, and the portfolio. Lead AI Agent strategy and implementation for large manufacturers, with limited supervision. From kickoff through expansion, you're the technical face of Nexus in the conference room and on the plant floor. You’ll own several relationships across multiple sites and implementations. Because you operate across industries, you'll spot the patterns a single-account engineer never sees. You'll turn an optimization proven in one plant into a playbook for ten, and connect what's happening on the factory floor to where the product needs to go.

Build agentic workflows that matter. Design and ship complex, large-scale agent workflows for use-cases like automated equipment root-cause analysis, production scheduling, and process optimization, work that directly moves the needle on revenue expansion and customer satisfaction, in environments running billions of dollars of product.

Move fast in slow places. Most Nexus deployments go live in under two weeks, in environments where enterprise software normally takes quarters. You'll meet each customer wherever they are on their data journey and get them to value fast.
Compound the platform. Every deployment makes Nexus better. You'll turn field learnings into reusable agents, connectors, and product feedback, so the next deployment is faster than the last, and so learnings from one industry compound into every other.

What You Bring:

Strong software engineering skills and real fluency with today's AI stack. You've built with LLMs, or you've gone deep enough on the tools and landscape to have strong opinions about what works.
The ability to handle ambiguity at portfolio scale - juggling multiple clients, sites, and implementations simultaneously, and synthesizing what you learn across them into insights that transfer between customers and industries.
Demonstrated excellence, through any combination of academic record, work experience, open-source contributions, or public writing.
Evidence of high agency and independent thinking - things you started, shipped, or wrote because nobody was going to do it for you.
You present well. You can own a customer relationship, run the room, and communicate hard technical ideas to plant managers and process engineers alike.
New grads welcome. This is an exceptional first role for someone who wants maximum ownership from day one.

Who You Are:

Excited about the promise of Physical AI and the people who keep the physical world running.
A pattern-seeker: energized by seeing how a fix in one vertical maps to a bottleneck in another, and by carrying those learnings across an entire book of customers.
Super driven - the kind of person who wants hands-on customer experience that could one day translate into your own startup or team.
At home in ambiguity: you'd rather figure out the right thing to build than be handed a spec.
A low-ego, high-integrity operator with an innate hunger to achieve goals in a startup environment.

Interview Process

Application review: Send us your stuff, and a quick note on why you're excited.
Intro chat: Share what you're looking for next and learn more about what we're building.
Founder interview: Talk with our founder in more detail about the role.
Technical interview: We'll have you complete a short exercise specific to the role.
Onsite: Come to San Francisco and meet the team through a series of 1:1 interviews.
Decision: We'll move fast.

This role is based in San Francisco, with regular travel to customer sites.

,

new_jobs.description:
Description

The Sponsored Products and Brands (SPB) team at Amazon Ads is re-imagining the advertising landscape through state-of-the-art generative AI technologies, revolutionizing how millions of customers discover products and engage with brands across Amazon.com and beyond. We are at the forefront of re-inventing advertising experiences, bridging human creativity with artificial intelligence to transform every aspect of the advertising lifecycle from ad creation and optimization to performance analysis and customer insights. We are a passionate group of innovators dedicated to developing responsible and intelligent AI technologies that balance the needs of advertisers, enhance the shopping experience, and strengthen the marketplace. If you're energized by solving complex challenges and pushing the boundaries of what's possible with AI, join us in shaping the future of advertising.

Key job responsibilities

Responsibilities

This role will be pivotal in redesigning how ads contribute to a personalized, relevant, and inspirational shopping experience, with the customer value proposition at the forefront. Key responsibilities include, but are not limited to:

Contribute to the design and development of GenAI, deep learning, multi-objective optimization and/or reinforcement learning empowered solutions to transform ad retrieval, auctions, whole-page relevance, and/or bespoke shopping experiences.
Collaborate cross-functionally with other scientists, engineers, and product managers to bring scalable, production-ready science solutions to life.
Stay abreast of industry trends in GenAI, LLMs, and related disciplines, bringing fresh and innovative concepts, ideas, and prototypes to the organization.
Contribute to the enhancement of team’s scientific and technical rigor by identifying and implementing best-in-class algorithms, methodologies, and infrastructure that enable rapid experimentation and scaling.
Mentor and grow junior scientists and engineers, cultivating a high-performing, collaborative, and intellectually curious team.

A day in the life

As an Applied Scientist on the Sponsored Products and Brands Off-Search team, you will contribute to the development in Generative AI (GenAI) and Large Language Models (LLMs) to revolutionize our advertising flow, backend optimization, and frontend shopping experiences. This is a rare opportunity to redefine how ads are retrieved, allocated, and/or experienced—elevating them into personalized, contextually aware, and inspiring components of the customer journey. You will have the opportunity to fundamentally transform areas such as ad retrieval, ad allocation, whole-page relevance, and differentiated recommendations through the lens of GenAI. By building novel generative models grounded in both Amazon’s rich data and the world’s collective knowledge, your work will shape how customers engage with ads, discover products, and make purchasing decisions. If you are passionate about applying frontier AI to real-world problems with massive scale and impact, this is your opportunity to define the next chapter of advertising science.

About The Team

The Off-Search team within Sponsored Products and Brands (SPB) is focused on building delightful ad experiences across various surfaces beyond Search on Amazon—such as product detail pages, the homepage, and store-in-store pages—to drive monetization. Our vision is to deliver highly personalized, context-aware advertising that adapts to individual shopper preferences, scales across diverse page types, remains relevant to seasonal and event-driven moments, and integrates seamlessly with organic recommendations such as new arrivals, basket-building content, and fast-delivery options. To execute this vision, we work in close partnership with Amazon Stores stakeholders to lead the expansion and growth of advertising across Amazon-owned and -operated pages beyond Search. We operate full stack—from backend ads-retail edge services, ads retrieval, and ad auctions to shopper-facing experiences—all designed to deliver meaningful value.

Curious about our advertising solutions? Discover more about Sponsored Products and Sponsored Brands to see how we’re helping businesses grow on Amazon.com and beyond!

Basic Qualifications

3+ years of building machine learning models for business application experience
PhD, or Master's degree and 6+ years of applied research experience
Experience programming in Java, C++, Python or related language
Strong foundation in GenAI, large language models, machine learning, deep learning, probabilistic modeling, and/or optimization.
Experience developing and deploying models in real-world production environments.

Preferred Qualifications

Proven expertise in Generative AI, foundation models, LLMs, and/or fine-tuning and customization for downstream tasks.
Hands-on experience in ads ranking, retrieval, recommendation systems, search, or personalization at web scale.
Deep understanding of multi-modal modeling, few-shot learning, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), or reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF).
Experience with online experimentation, A/B testing frameworks, and metrics design for advertising or e-commerce.
Demonstrated ability to communicate complex technical topics clearly to both technical and non-technical audiences.
Experience in computational advertising, including familiarity with auction theory, ad economics, and advertiser performance metrics.

new_jobs.title: AI Engineer II
new_jobs.description:
Our Deloitte Human Capital team transforms technology platforms, drives innovation, and helps make a significant impact on our clients' success. We are hiring an AI Engineer to build and operate the data, features, and GenAI foundations that power Human Capital AI products and analytics. You will work with an AI Data Engineer (data ingestion, curation, governance, platform foundations) and a Lead AI Solutions Architect (end-to-end solution architecture, integration patterns, non-functional requirements), partnering closely with product, data science/ML, security, and platform engineering to deliver reliable, secure, and scalable AI solutions.

This role is hands-on and delivery-oriented: you will ship production pipelines and services that support model training, real-time inference, and LLM applications using Claude-, GPT/Codex-, Gemini-class, and other models, with strong governance, observability, and cost/performance discipline.

Recruiting for this role ends on 10/30/2026.

Work you'll do

As an AI and Data Science Engineer II on the HC Forward team, you will be responsible for designing, building, and running the trusted, governed data, feature, and retrieval layer used by artificial intelligence/machine learning (AI/ML) and generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) solutions. You will deliver reproducible datasets and features, operationalize quality and lineage, and enable secure consumption patterns for predictive machine learning (ML) and large language model (LLM)-based experiences.

Partner with the Lead AI Solutions Architect and AI Data Engineer to translate Human Capital product needs into secure, scalable technical designs and delivered solutions, including application programming interfaces (APIs), services, pipelines, and containers/serverless solutions that meet availability, performance, and security expectations.
Build and operationalize LLM-enabled capabilities, including copilots, human resources (HR) knowledge assistants, summarization, and policy question-and-answer experiences, using Claude/GPT(Codex)/Gemini, including secure endpoints, tool/function calling, and reusable prompt/context patterns.
Implement LLM application patterns, including retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), document ingestion/chunking, embeddings, vector/hybrid search, and retrieval/evaluation telemetry.
Deliver governed datasets and feature engineering/serving for ML training and real-time inference, including online/offline consistency, caching, latency service-level objectives (SLOs), and backfills.
Operationalize data quality and lineage and enable secure consumption patterns for predictive ML and LLM-based experiences.

A successful candidate would possess these skills:

Ability to work independently and collaborate as part of a team
Effective written and verbal communication skills
Meticulous attention to detail and quality of work product
Ability to build and sustain professional relationships
Ability to lead projects or workstreams
Ability to manage and prioritize multiple tasks in a fast-paced and dynamic environment
Strong interpersonal skills and professional demeanor
Ability to meet deadlines
Ability to provide clear guidance to others

The team

HC Forward is a dedicated innovation partner accelerating the future of Human Capital by building market-aligned products, platforms, and services that apply AI, data, and engineering to modernize HR experiences and outcomes.

Qualifications

Required:

Bachelor's degree in a STEM field (e.g., Computer Science, Engineering, Statistics, Data Science)
2+ years building and delivering large language model (LLM) and generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) solutions with Claude/GPT(Codex)/Gemini-class models, including prompt/context design, tool/function calling, evaluation, and production integration; and 2+ years implementing retrieval-augmented generation (RAG)/retrieval, including document processing, embeddings, vector/hybrid search, and enterprise governance controls.
2+ years of data and artificial intelligence engineering, including data modeling, batch/streaming pipelines, structured/unstructured processing, and feature engineering/serving fundamentals; and 2+ years building production, real-time inference services, including application programming interface (API) design, latency/performance, and reliability patterns.
2+ years leading platform/integration engineering across enterprise systems, including API/integration experience with Representational State Transfer (REST), GraphQL, event-driven capabilities, microservices, and middleware; and 2+ years of development operations (DevOps) and development, security, and operations (DevSecOps) experience, including continuous integration/continuous delivery (CI/CD), infrastructure as code (IaC) using Terraform/CloudFormation, Docker/Kubernetes, observability, and monitoring.
2+ years leading security/compliance efforts, including enterprise security controls-identity and access management (IAM), encryption, secrets, and audit logging-and data/privacy controls-personally identifiable information (PII), retention, and access controls.
Ability to travel 0-25%, on average, based on the work you do and the clients and industries/sectors you serve.
Must be legally authorized to work in the United States without the need for employer sponsorship, now or at any time in the future.

Preferred:

Master's or doctoral degree and/or cloud and artificial intelligence/machine learning (AI/ML) certifications.
2+ years of experience with Human Capital platforms and integrations, including Workday, SAP SuccessFactors, Oracle HCM, Salesforce, and human resources (HR) data domains.
2+ years of experience operationalizing large language model operations (LLMOps) and machine learning operations (MLOps) capabilities, including evaluation, monitoring, governance workflows, and model/prompt/version management; and 2+ years of cloud experience with one or more of Amazon Web Services (AWS), Microsoft Azure, or Google Cloud Platform (GCP), including managed data platforms and compute patterns.
2+ years translating business needs into documented requirements, acceptance criteria, and shippable increments using structured problem solving; and 2+ years documenting and communicating AI/GenAI trade-offs involving quality, latency, cost, and risk to stakeholders.
2+ years collaborating across product, data science/machine learning, data engineering, platform, and security functions; and 2+ years performing threat testing, monitoring, and operational-readiness responsibilities.
2+ years applying ethics and privacy practices to recognize consent, personally identifiable information (PII), and bias boundaries and escalate concerns; and experience with System and Organization Controls (SOC) 2, the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR), or the Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA).

The wage range for this role takes into account the wide range of factors that are considered in making compensation decisions including but not limited to skill sets; experience and training; licensure and certifications; and other business and organizational needs. The disclosed range estimate has not been adjusted for the applicable geographic differential associated with the location at which the position may be filled. At Deloitte, it is not typical for an individual to be hired at or near the top of the range for their role and compensation decisions are dependent on the facts and circumstances of each case. A reasonable estimate of the current range is $91,100 to $179,500.

A Master's or PhD in Linguistics, Cognitive Science, or a related field

4+ years of experience in large-scale experiment design and quantitative research projects in an industry setting or applied research

You will work with an AI Data Engineer (data ingestion, curation, governance, platform foundations) and a Lead AI Solutions Architect (end-to-end solution architecture, integration patterns, non-functional requirements), partnering closely with product, data science/ML, security, and platform engineering to deliver reliable, secure, and scalable AI solutions.

This role is hands-on and delivery-oriented: you will ship production pipelines and services that support model training, real-time inference, and LLM applications using Claude-, GPT/Codex-, Gemini-class, and other models, with strong governance, observability, and cost/performance discipline.

Recruiting for this role ends on 10/30/2026.

Work you'll do

As an AI and Data Science Engineer II on the HC Forward team, you will be responsible for designing, building, and running the trusted, governed data, feature, and retrieval layer used by artificial intelligence/machine learning (AI/ML) and generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) solutions. You will deliver reproducible datasets and features, operationalize quality and lineage, and enable secure consumption patterns for predictive machine learning (ML) and large language model (LLM)-based experiences.

Partner with the Lead AI Solutions Architect and AI Data Engineer to translate Human Capital product needs into secure, scalable technical designs and delivered solutions, including application programming interfaces (APIs), services, pipelines, and containers/serverless solutions that meet availability, performance, and security expectations.
Build and operationalize LLM-enabled capabilities, including copilots, human resources (HR) knowledge assistants, summarization, and policy question-and-answer experiences, using Claude/GPT(Codex)/Gemini, including secure endpoints, tool/function calling, and reusable prompt/context patterns.
Implement LLM application patterns, including retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), document ingestion/chunking, embeddings, vector/hybrid search, and retrieval/evaluation telemetry.
Deliver governed datasets and feature engineering/serving for ML training and real-time inference, including online/offline consistency, caching, latency service-level objectives (SLOs), and backfills.
Operationalize data quality and lineage and enable secure consumption patterns for predictive ML and LLM-based experiences.

A successful candidate would possess these skills:

Ability to work independently and collaborate as part of a team
Effective written and verbal communication skills
Meticulous attention to detail and quality of work product
Ability to build and sustain professional relationships
Ability to lead projects or workstreams
Ability to manage and prioritize multiple tasks in a fast-paced and dynamic environment
Strong interpersonal skills and professional demeanor
Ability to meet deadlines
Ability to provide clear guidance to others

The team

HC Forward is a dedicated innovation partner accelerating the future of Human Capital by building market-aligned products, platforms, and services that apply AI, data, and engineering to modernize HR experiences and outcomes.

Qualifications

Required:

Bachelor's degree in a STEM field (e.g., Computer Science, Engineering, Statistics, Data Science)
2+ years building and delivering large language model (LLM) and generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) solutions with Claude/GPT(Codex)/Gemini-class models, including prompt/context design, tool/function calling, evaluation, and production integration; and 2+ years implementing retrieval-augmented generation (RAG)/retrieval, including document processing, embeddings, vector/hybrid search, and enterprise governance controls.
2+ years of data and artificial intelligence engineering, including data modeling, batch/streaming pipelines, structured/unstructured processing, and feature engineering/serving fundamentals; and 2+ years building production, real-time inference services, including application programming interface (API) design, latency/performance, and reliability patterns.
2+ years leading platform/integration engineering across enterprise systems, including API/integration experience with Representational State Transfer (REST), GraphQL, event-driven capabilities, microservices, and middleware; and 2+ years of development operations (DevOps) and development, security, and operations (DevSecOps) experience, including continuous integration/continuous delivery (CI/CD), infrastructure as code (IaC) using Terraform/CloudFormation, Docker/Kubernetes, observability, and monitoring.
2+ years leading security/compliance efforts, including enterprise security controls-identity and access management (IAM), encryption, secrets, and audit logging-and data/privacy controls-personally identifiable information (PII), retention, and access controls.
Ability to travel 0-25%, on average, based on the work you do and the clients and industries/sectors you serve.
Must be legally authorized to work in the United States without the need for employer sponsorship, now or at any time in the future.

Preferred:

Master's or doctoral degree and/or cloud and artificial intelligence/machine learning (AI/ML) certifications.
2+ years of experience with Human Capital platforms and integrations, including Workday, SAP SuccessFactors, Oracle HCM, Salesforce, and human resources (HR) data domains.
2+ years of experience operationalizing large language model operations (LLMOps) and machine learning operations (MLOps) capabilities, including evaluation, monitoring, governance workflows, and model/prompt/version management; and 2+ years of cloud experience with one or more of Amazon Web Services (AWS), Microsoft Azure, or Google Cloud Platform (GCP), including managed data platforms and compute patterns.
2+ years translating business needs into documented requirements, acceptance criteria, and shippable increments using structured problem solving; and 2+ years documenting and communicating AI/GenAI trade-offs involving quality, latency, cost, and risk to stakeholders.
2+ years collaborating across product, data science/machine learning, data engineering, platform, and security functions; and 2+ years performing threat testing, monitoring, and operational-readiness responsibilities.
2+ years applying ethics and privacy practices to recognize consent, personally identifiable information (PII), and bias boundaries and escalate concerns; and experience with System and Organization Controls (SOC) 2, the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR), or the Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA).

new_jobs.description:
About Us

Manufact builds dev-tools and cloud infrastructure for MCP and software used by AI agents.

Our platform helps teams build, deploy, test, and distribute MCP servers and apps across ChatGPT, Claude, Muse, Grok Bot, and other AI agents.

We created mcp-use SDK, the Next.js for MCP, with 10k GitHub stars and 10M+ downloads
. We’re backed by Y Combinator (S25)
and a $6.3M seed round led by Peak XV
, with investors including the founders of Supabase.

We believe every software company will need an agent interface, just as it needs a website today.

About The Role

We’re hiring our first Forward Deployed Engineer to help enterprise customers and partners go from an idea to a product running on Manufact.

You’ll work across enterprise pilots, technical partnerships and customer success. One week you might build an integration with another developer tool. The next, you’ll help a consulting partner deploy its first customer’s MCP app or get an enterprise implementation into production.

You own the technical journey from discovery through launch and adoption. That means writing code, making architecture decisions, working directly with customers, and making sure everyone follows through.

Your work is successful when the customer is actually using the product and getting value from it.

What you’ll own

Technical discovery and pilots. Understand the use case, define success criteria, scope the solution and build a working proof of concept.
Implementation through production. Build MCP servers, apps and integrations. Debug APIs, authentication and deployment issues. Test the complete flow and help customers launch.
Customer delivery. Treat implementation as an important feature delivery. Maintain a shared implementation roadmap, give every task an owner, run weekly check-ins, and hold both teams accountable for agreed commitments.
Technical customer success. Stay close after launch. Monitor adoption, resolve blockers and help customers expand their usage.
Partner engineering. Work with developer tools, system integrators and consultants to ship integrations and enable their teams to deliver on Manufact.
Make the next deployment easier. Turn repeated work into templates, documentation, reusable integrations and product improvements.

You’ll work directly with the founders and our product, infrastructure and DevRel teams, with ownership of technical delivery and customer adoption.

Who you are

You’ve shipped software used by real customers and can explain what happened after launch.
Strong TypeScript skills and experience with APIs, authentication, integrations and cloud deployment.
Comfortable moving between a customer call, a technical design, your editor and production debugging.
You take ownership. When something stalls, you identify the blocker, find the right owner and follow through.
Clear written and verbal communication. You can explain trade-offs to engineers and business stakeholders.
Good judgment about what to build, what to reuse and when to involve the core engineering team.
Based in or willing to relocate to San Francisco.

Experience in forward-deployed engineering, solutions engineering, partner engineering or an early-stage engineering team is useful. What matters most is evidence that you can build and get customers live.

Nice to have

Experience with MCP, AI agents, developer tools or infrastructure.
Python experience.
Enterprise implementations or technical customer success.
Open-source contributions or technical writing.

What you can expect

Work directly with the founders and shape a new function.
Equity.
Premium medical and dependent coverage.
Unlimited PTO.
401(k) with company match.
Relocation assistance.

new_jobs.title: Forward Deployed Engineer
new_jobs.description:
Build with enterprise customers, own the path to production, and turn repeated lessons into a better product.

About Sycamore

Sycamore is building the trusted agent operating system for the enterprise. Our platform helps companies build, deploy, and orchestrate agentic apps that take on real operational work, with the security and control large organizations need.

We are a small, engineering-led team working directly with Fortune 500 enterprises. We have raised $65M from Coatue and Lightspeed, along with other investors and industry leaders.

The role

The simplest way to describe this role: you are the engineer in the customer room and the product engineer who ships what the room needs. You will map how an important workflow works today, find where an agent can create a measurable outcome, and build the application end to end, from the user experience and data model through agent tools, integrations, permissions, approval points, and the operational controls needed to run safely.

You own the full loop: discovery, implementation, realistic testing, deployment, production debugging, adoption, and iteration. Customer-specific product work belongs with you, and when the same runtime, connector, memory, or deployment need appears repeatedly, you work with Core AI or Infrastructure to turn it into a reusable capability rather than maintaining parallel custom implementations.

What you will do

Turn ambiguous enterprise problems into clear technical designs, working software, and measurable outcomes.
Build product surfaces for agent conversations, tasks, progress, approvals, artifacts, and operational workflows.
Design APIs and relational data models that accurately represent the customer’s domain and remain understandable as the product evolves.
Build agent instructions, tool interfaces, connector interactions, and durable workflow steps with explicit permission and failure behavior.
Navigate enterprise requirements around authentication, authorization, tenant isolation, data handling, deployment, observability, and change management.
Test realistic user journeys rather than stopping at isolated units or happy-path demos.
Travel to customer sites when working alongside users will accelerate discovery, delivery, or adoption.

The environment you will work in

Our current product environment includes TypeScript, React, TanStack, Tailwind, Python, FastAPI, typed data models, PostgreSQL, durable workflows, MCP-based tools and connectors, browser automation, and cloud-native deployment on Kubernetes.

We use automated tests, coding agents, traces, evaluations, and production feedback as part of everyday engineering.

This is context, not a checklist. We do not require previous experience with every language, framework, or vendor in our stack. Strong engineers who understand systems, learn quickly, and have shipped production software can become effective here without matching our tools one for one.

What we are looking for

5-12 years of software engineering experience. We will make exceptions for exceptional people in either direction.
Strong software fundamentals across product design, APIs, data modeling, distributed systems, testing, and production debugging.
Evidence that you personally shipped and operated meaningful software, rather than stopping at prototypes or delegating the production work.
Product judgment. You can find the real problem behind a request, choose a useful first version, and decide what should remain customer-specific versus become reusable.
Comfort moving across user interfaces, backend services, data, agent behavior, integrations, and deployment when the outcome requires it.
A security-minded approach to enterprise data, permissions, credentials, approvals, and auditability.
AI-native. You use coding agents and modern models as a force multiplier while still owning the architecture, understanding the code, and explaining important decisions.
Clear communication and high EQ. You can work with a customer’s CTO, operators, security team, and engineers without losing technical depth.
Comfort with startup ambiguity, fast feedback loops, broad ownership, and regular customer travel.

Former founders, early product engineers, and forward-deployed engineers often do well here when they have retained real code and production ownership. That background is a signal, not a requirement.

What this role is not

It is not a pre-sales role that stops at a demo or architecture diagram.
It is not a solutions role that hands requirements to another engineering team.
It is not custom development without product judgment; repeated needs should improve the platform.

Interview process

A 30-minute introductory conversation.
Two 60-minute technical interviews, one focused on systems design and one on coding.
A take-home assignment where you build and present a real solution using the tools you would use on the job.

Why join

Work on AI systems that move from enterprise problems to production outcomes quickly.
Own the complete path from workflow discovery through adoption.
Shape both individual deployments and the product used across customers.
Join early enough to define how the engineering team operates and grows.
Receive competitive cash compensation and meaningful equity in the company you are helping build.

new_jobs.title: Senior Staff AI-Native DevOps Engineer
new_jobs.description:
Company Description

It all started when engineer Fred Luddy wrote code that automated a tedious task for his coworker, Phyllis. She cried tears of joy. That moment inspired Fred to build a company that could do that for everyone—freeing people from busywork so they could focus on meaningful work. Today, ServiceNow is the AI control tower for business reinvention. Our ServiceNow AI platform brings together any AI, any data, and any workflow— helping 85% of the Fortune 500® work smarter, faster, and better. We're building an AI-native culture where technology and talent are unstoppable together. And we're just getting started.

Join us to put AI to work for people.

Job Description

About the team

The Conversational AI team at ServiceNow builds the core platform behind ServiceNow Otto, our conversational AI experience. We are a group of applied scientists and software engineers working at the intersection of research and production. Our work spans the full stack that makes Otto capable: agent orchestration, including harness engineering, prompt tuning, agent skills, policy design, and quality evaluation across languages; the A2A and MCP protocols that let agents collaborate and connect to tools; background channels and conversational triggers that bring agents into action; AI-native licensing and pricing; and the central caching layer that connects the ServiceNow platform to the services powering Otto.

We are seeking a Staff AI-Native DevOps Engineer
to lead a new DevOps practice within the Conversational AI team. You will own the build, deployment, and reliability of the systems behind ServiceNow Otto, our conversational AI platform, from commit through production across our SaaS environments. Your work will span CI/CD pipelines, release automation, infrastructure on Kubernetes, observability, and the operational tooling that lets agent orchestration, MCP and A2A services, and the central caching layer ship safely and frequently. You will partner closely with applied scientists and software engineers to make AI-native delivery repeatable, measurable, and secure. This role combines deep expertise in cloud infrastructure, containerization, orchestration, and infrastructure as code with a practical understanding of how ML and LLM-based services behave in production, and a bias toward pragmatic engineering with measurable impact on deployment velocity and service reliability.

Qualifications

To be successful in this role you have:

Deep expertise in designing, building, and operating scalable, reliable, and secure cloud-native applications and infrastructure.
Strong software engineering skills, with experience developing infrastructure tooling and automation using Go, Python, or similar languages.
Experience leading complex infrastructure initiatives, establishing engineering best practices, and driving adoption across multiple teams.
Strong problem-solving skills, with the ability to diagnose complex distributed systems issues and drive improvements in performance, reliability, and operational efficiency.
Strong understanding of modern AI technologies, including Large Language Models (LLMs), Generative AI, and agentic architectures, with the ability to apply these concepts to engineering and operational challenges.
An AI-native engineering mindset, proactively leveraging AI tools and automation to accelerate development, improve operational efficiency, and deliver more intelligent, resilient systems.

DevOps

Deploy, scale, and operate distributed microservices in production Kubernetes environments, including managing application lifecycle, networking, security, and service reliability.
Design and implement infrastructure automation using Infrastructure as Code (IaC) and Kubernetes-native tooling, including Terraform, Ansible, Helm, and Kubernetes Operators.
Build and maintain CI/CD pipelines and GitOps workflows using tools such as Jenkins, GitHub Actions, Tekton, and ArgoCD to automate testing, deployment, and release management.
Implement observability, monitoring, and incident response practices, performing root cause analysis and driving remediation to improve availability, fault tolerance, and operational resilience.
Architect and optimize cloud infrastructure across public and private cloud environments, with an emphasis on security, scalability, cost efficiency, and operational simplicity.

AI Skills

Artificial intelligence strategy is a critical skill at your level — it applies to how you build and to what you build.

Confident use of AI coding assistants such as GitHub Copilot or Cursor, paired with the critical eye to review AI-generated code as rigorously as any other — catching logic errors, security anti-patterns, and missed edge cases rather than treating model output as production-ready.
AI-assisted debugging and trace analysis, and a clear understanding of the data privacy rules governing what goes into a prompt.
Understanding of LLM-powered application architectures, including model inference, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), tool calling, and agentic workflows, with an awareness of their infrastructure, scalability, and reliability implications.
Ability to deploy, operate, and troubleshoot AI-powered services in production, including managing model API integrations, observability, latency, resource utilization, and operational costs.

Minimum Requirements

8+ years of professional software engineering, infrastructure engineering, DevOps, or related experience.
6+ years of experience deploying and operating containerized applications and distributed services in production environments.
4+ years of hands-on experience with Kubernetes, cloud infrastructure, and infrastructure automation.
Proficiency in at least one programming or scripting language, such as Go, Python, or Bash, with experience building production-grade automation and tooling.
Practical experience using AI-assisted development tools in software engineering workflows, with demonstrated ability to validate, debug, and safely integrate AI-generated code.
Working knowledge of LLMs, Generative AI, and agentic AI concepts, including their integration patterns and operational considerations.

Preferred Requirements

12+ years of experience in software engineering, infrastructure engineering, DevOps, or platform engineering.

new_jobs.description:
Do you want your voice heard and your actions to count?

Discover your opportunity with Mitsubishi UFJ Financial Group (MUFG), one of the world’s leading financial groups. Across the globe, we’re 150,000 colleagues, striving to make a difference for every client, organization, and community we serve. We stand for our values, building long-term relationships, serving society, and fostering shared and sustainable growth for a better world.

With a vision to be the world’s most trusted financial group, it’s part of our culture to put people first, listen to new and diverse ideas and collaborate toward greater innovation, speed and agility. This means investing in talent, technologies, and tools that empower you to own your career.

Join MUFG, where being inspired is expected and making a meaningful impact is rewarded.

The selected colleague will work at an MUFG office or client sites four days per week and work remotely one day. A member of our recruitment team will provide more details.

The Global Talent, Learning & Culture team is responsible for a range of key HR areas and processes across the Global MUFG Bank and Securities business; including Learning & Development, Talent Management, Talent Acquisition & Mobility, and Culture & Engagement.

The role of Talent, Learning & Culture (TL&C) is to ensure that MUFG maintains a high performing workforce, and is an organization where people can join, accelerate, learn, develop and progress their careers alongside their personal goals. The team aims to provide sound expert advice and resources to both HR and business colleagues, and to deliver programs that support the development of highly performing and engaged teams.

The VP, AI Learning & Development Lead – Americas will shape and execute the Americas- wide AI workforce enablement roadmap, translating evolving AI capabilities and business needs into practical, role-based learning and adoption opportunities. The role will combine strong AI fluency and hands-on experience with enterprise generative AI tools and delivering AI Learning & Development programs to build workforce capability, enable practical use of AI, and help embed new ways of working across the region.

The role will lead cross-functional coordination across TL&C, Technology/IT, PMO, Corporate Communications, Risk, Legal, Compliance, Procurement, vendors, Business Unit AI Leads, HRBPs, and business stakeholders to align priorities, manage dependencies, and move the program from strategy through implementation.

Strategy, AI Enablement & Learning Design

Establish the AI capability framework and learning architecture for the Americas, aligned to global foundations and adapted for regional business, technology, and regulatory requirements.
Define target audiences, proficiency levels, and desired outcomes, including pathways for novice, intermediate, advanced/expert, senior leader, people manager, technical, and champion populations.
Translate AI capabilities, business needs, and SME input into role-based learning pathways, instructor-led opportunities, clear learning objectives, and practical guidance for technical and non-technical audiences.
Define the baseline proficiency approach and mandatory AI learning & development plan for all employees.
Leverage and adapt existing global capability frameworks, audience segmentation, supplier criteria, learning architecture, current state/gap analysis, and governance approaches.
Make recommendations to build, buy, reuse, or adapt learning solutions by evaluating internal and external offerings against capability and business requirements.
Assess business demand, capability gaps, and emerging AI use cases through partnership with Business Unit AI Leads, HRBPs, Technology, and business stakeholders.
Coordinate with Risk, Legal, and Compliance to incorporate requirements associated with new AI tools, capabilities, and use cases.
Maintain strong fluency in emerging AI capabilities, tools, use cases, and workforce trends, translating relevant developments into practical learning and enablement opportunities for the Americas.

Program Leadership & Stakeholder Engagement

Lead the cross-functional AI learning & development program across TL&C, PMO, Technology/IT, Procurement, Risk, Legal, Compliance, Corporate Communications, vendors, Business Unit AI Leads, HRBPs, and business stakeholders across MUFG’s bank, securities, trust bank, and investor services entities in the Americas region.
Translate evolving AI workforce priorities into a connected roadmap and implementation plan, leading the program structure, stakeholder alignment, decision points, and follow-through required to drive execution.
Manage dependencies across content and SME readiness, platform access, procurement, supplier decisions, regulatory input, communications timing, implementation capacity, and emerging business use cases.
Establish sustainable governance and intake processes to prioritize business-unit-specific workforce enablement requirements and AI use cases.
Partner with global and regional TL&C stakeholders, including the EMEA AI Workforce Enablement lead and APAC workstreams, to leverage existing frameworks, maintain global alignment, and adapt solutions for the Americas.
Act as a trusted partner to business and functional stakeholders, facilitating alignment and proactively managing priorities, timelines, dependencies, decisions, and implementation readiness.
Establish program reporting and adoption governance, including training completions, Copilot usage, champion engagement, and pulse results for senior stakeholders.

Execution & Adoption

Coordinate implementation and delivery of selected learning solutions, including self-paced content, assessments, curated pathways, instructor-led options, and measurement support.
Execute role-based learning pathways, instructor-led opportunities, employee self-learning engagement, and mandatory baseline learning & development plan.
Own, deploy, and sustain practical learning and enablement resources, including people leader toolkits, office hours, FAQs, playbooks, and workflow-based guidance that help employees apply AI effectively in their work.
Partner with relevant business owners on learning vendor engagement, including detailed vendor inquiries and evaluation inputs.
Create ongoing feedback loops across senior stakeholders, employee peer groups, and the broader employee base to inform learning priorities, use cases, and adoption.
Support peer-to-peer employee groups with onboarding, quarterly sessions, operating cadence, recognition, and toolkits.
Coordinate with responsible SMEs, platform owners, communications partners, and business stakeholders to enable new AI tools and capabilities based on business need.
Proactively develop PMO and stakeholder updates, governance materials, leadership-ready content, and implementation communications in partnership with Corporate Communications.

Experience

Proven track record leading large-scale, complex programs across multiple businesses, legal entities, and geographies.
Demonstrated experience across Learning & Development, digital adoption, program management, workforce transformation, or related roles.
Direct experience leading an enterprise AI or digital enablement program with Technology partners, from tool rollout through adoption.
Proven experience designing, implementing, or scaling learning and adoption programs that build capability, drive behavior change, and enable new ways of working.
Hands-on experience with enterprise generative AI tools (e.g., Microsoft 365 Copilot, agent builders).
Technology and learning and development vendor management experience.

Confidence with advanced or niche AI tools and use cases, including agents, custom AI solutions, and workflow-based AI enablement.
Program leadership: Strong program leadership skills, including translating evolving or ambiguous priorities into a clear roadmap, coordinating multiple workstreams and cross-functional dependencies, and driving execution end-to-end with limited oversight.

Company Description

It all started when engineer Fred Luddy wrote code that automated a tedious task for his coworker, Phyllis. She cried tears of joy. That moment inspired Fred to build a company that could do that for everyone—freeing people from busywork so they could focus on meaningful work. Today, ServiceNow is the AI control tower for business reinvention. Our ServiceNow AI platform brings together any AI, any data, and any workflow— helping 85% of the Fortune 500® work smarter, faster, and better. We're building an AI-native culture where technology and talent are unstoppable together. And we're just getting started.

Join us to put AI to work for people.

Job Description

About the team

The Conversational AI team at ServiceNow builds the core platform behind ServiceNow Otto, our conversational AI experience. We are a group of applied scientists and software engineers working at the intersection of research and production. Our work spans the full stack that makes Otto capable: agent orchestration, including harness engineering, prompt tuning, agent skills, policy design, and quality evaluation across languages; the A2A and MCP protocols that let agents collaborate and connect to tools; background channels and conversational triggers that bring agents into action; AI-native licensing and pricing; and the central caching layer that connects the ServiceNow platform to the services powering Otto.

We are seeking a Staff AI-Native DevOps Engineer
to join a new DevOps practice within the Conversational AI team. You will own the build, deployment, and reliability of the systems behind ServiceNow Otto, our conversational AI platform, from commit through production across our SaaS environments. Your work will span CI/CD pipelines, release automation, infrastructure on Kubernetes, observability, and the operational tooling that lets agent orchestration, MCP and A2A services, and the central caching layer ship safely and frequently. You will partner closely with applied scientists and software engineers to make AI-native delivery repeatable, measurable, and secure. This role combines deep expertise in cloud infrastructure, containerization, orchestration, and infrastructure as code with a practical understanding of how ML and LLM-based services behave in production, and a bias toward pragmatic engineering with measurable impact on deployment velocity and service reliability.

Qualifications

To be successful in this role you have:

Deep expertise in designing, building, and operating scalable, reliable, and secure cloud-native applications and infrastructure.
Strong software engineering skills, with experience developing infrastructure tooling and automation using Go, Python, or similar languages.
Experience leading complex infrastructure initiatives, establishing engineering best practices, and driving adoption across multiple teams.
Strong problem-solving skills, with the ability to diagnose complex distributed systems issues and drive improvements in performance, reliability, and operational efficiency.
Strong understanding of modern AI technologies, including Large Language Models (LLMs), Generative AI, and agentic architectures, with the ability to apply these concepts to engineering and operational challenges.
An AI-native engineering mindset, proactively leveraging AI tools and automation to accelerate development, improve operational efficiency, and deliver more intelligent, resilient systems.

Deploy, scale, and operate distributed microservices in production Kubernetes environments, including managing application lifecycle, networking, security, and service reliability.
Design and implement infrastructure automation using Infrastructure as Code (IaC) and Kubernetes-native tooling, including Terraform, Ansible, Helm, and Kubernetes Operators.
Build and maintain CI/CD pipelines and GitOps workflows using tools such as Jenkins, GitHub Actions, Tekton, and ArgoCD to automate testing, deployment, and release management.
Implement observability, monitoring, and incident response practices, performing root cause analysis and driving remediation to improve availability, fault tolerance, and operational resilience.
Architect and optimize cloud infrastructure across public and private cloud environments, with an emphasis on security, scalability, cost efficiency, and operational simplicity.

AI Skills

Artificial intelligence strategy is a critical skill at your level — it applies to how you build and to what you build.

Confident use of AI coding assistants such as GitHub Copilot or Cursor, paired with the critical eye to review AI-generated code as rigorously as any other — catching logic errors, security anti-patterns, and missed edge cases rather than treating model output as production-ready.
AI-assisted debugging and trace analysis, and a clear understanding of the data privacy rules governing what goes into a prompt.
Understanding of LLM-powered application architectures, including model inference, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), tool calling, and agentic workflows, with an awareness of their infrastructure, scalability, and reliability implications.
Ability to deploy, operate, and troubleshoot AI-powered services in production, including managing model API integrations, observability, latency, resource utilization, and operational costs.

Practical experience using AI-assisted development tools in software engineering workflows, with demonstrated ability to validate, debug, and safely integrate AI-generated code.
Working knowledge of LLMs, Generative AI, and agentic AI concepts, including their integration patterns and operational considerations.

new_jobs.title: Applied AI Engineer, Startups (Life Sciences)
new_jobs.description:
About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About The Role

As an Applied AI Engineer on the Startups team at Anthropic, you will be a trusted technical advisor to the top AI-native life sciences and biotech startups as they grow from early product to scale. Some of these companies build products on Claude that they sell to the rest of the industry, and others do the science themselves and want Claude woven into how their own research runs, and this role works with both. You'll lead deep technical engagements, partnering directly with startup engineering and scientific teams to help them build their products on Claude and run their own research with it, advising on implementation and agent design as they build what is newly possible with AI in the life sciences. You will bridge the gap between what Claude can do and what the life sciences need, working alongside some of the strongest teams in the field on problems that matter and pushing the boundaries of AI in science as you go.

Working closely with Applied AI Architects, Account Executives, and Anthropic's Product, Engineering, and Research teams, you'll help startups build at the edge of what is possible with Claude. You'll leverage your AI engineering expertise and your scientific domain knowledge to develop custom evaluation frameworks, design scalable architectures, and create the technical resources that enable life sciences startups to succeed with Claude.

Responsibilities

Serve as a deep technical advisor to high-potential life sciences and biotech startups, whether Claude sits inside the product they sell or inside the way they make discoveries, working alongside them to build innovative use cases that push the boundaries of AI in scientific research and development
Work hands-on with startup engineering teams and their scientists through pair programming and architecture reviews that accelerate their development, and understand their scientific workflows end to end so that your guidance fits into real research pipelines
Develop prototypes and technical documentation, including evaluation suites, scientifically grounded benchmarks, AI engineering techniques, and architecture diagrams, that enable startups to build, operate, and scale with Claude
Create reference implementations and sample code that many companies can adopt without starting from scratch, such as example MCP servers for domain-specific data sources like genomics platforms, literature databases, and experimental repositories, along with agent skills for common scientific workflows
Collaborate closely with Applied AI Architects to maintain context and continuity across customer engagements
Identify patterns across engagements, including what is hard about deploying AI in the life sciences such as heterogeneous data, auditability requirements, and the gap between a working prototype and a system that scientists trust, and contribute insights back to Product, Engineering, Research, and the broader Applied AI team, including feedback on the model capabilities and product features that would most accelerate discovery work
Create technical content for startup audiences including documentation, tutorials, and sample code
Represent Anthropic across the life sciences startup ecosystem and foster community engagement through hackathons, webinars, technical office hours, in-person founder events, and research show and tells
Travel to customer sites for workshops, implementation guidance, and relationship building

You may be a good fit if you have

Deep experience in the life sciences or biotech, gained through research or industry work in areas such as genomics, drug discovery, molecular design, lab automation, or clinical development, along with strong opinions of your own about how to bridge the gap between what AI can do today and what the life sciences need
4+ years of technical experience as a software engineer, ML or research engineer, computational biologist, research scientist, or technical founder, with either production experience building LLM-powered applications, including prompting, context engineering, agent architectures, evaluation frameworks, and deployment at scale, or a track record of successfully applying AI to real scientific work in the lab or in research
Experience with startups or high-growth companies and a love of working with founders and small teams that move quickly
Strong technical communication skills, with the ability to translate complex AI concepts into architectural decisions and actionable implementation plans for both engineering and scientific audiences and to run technical workshops, hackathons, or developer-focused events
A collaborative approach to working across teams, the ability to context-switch across scientific domains and use cases, and a passion for making powerful technology safe and beneficial

The annual compensation range for this role is listed below.

For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role.

Annual Salary

$280,000—$320,000 USD

Logistics

Minimum education:
Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience

Required field of study:
A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience

Minimum years of experience:
Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position

Location-based hybrid policy:
Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices.

Visa sponsorship:
We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this.

We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification.
Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team.

Your safety matters to us.
To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings.

How We're Different

We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills.

The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences.

Come work with us!

Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. Learn about our policy for using AI in our application process.

A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience

Minimum years of experience:
Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position

Location-based hybrid policy:
Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices.

Visa sponsorship:
We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this.

We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification.
Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team.

Your safety matters to us.
To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings.

How We're Different

We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills.

The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences.

Come work with us!

Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues.
